title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding and agent tool being used outside the conditions its developers anticipated. Cursor Agent, which runs Claude Sonnet as its underlying model, was directed by ransomware operators to carry out standard exploitation tasks: installing VPN clients, running network scans, enumerating domain privileges, and attempting credential-relay attacks. The tool was not compromised or modified, it was simply operated as intended, with the operators supplying the instructions and the agent executing them against victim infrastructure.

The failure mode is misuse of a legitimately accessed tool rather than a vulnerability in the AI model itself. Nothing in the reporting establishes that Cursor Agent had guardrails capable of distinguishing authorized penetration testing from criminal intrusion, and the tasks it was asked to perform, network scanning, privilege enumeration, are also routine in legitimate security work. The gap exploited was the absence of any check, inside the tool or outside it, on who was issuing commands and toward what end.

What is not established is whether Anysphere, the company behind Cursor, had any knowledge of this use, or whether the operators obtained access through a paid account, a trial, or some other means. The reporting documents observed behavior attributed with medium confidence to a second cluster, and attribution at that confidence level is an analytical judgment, not a confirmed finding.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group has been actively targeting organizations since April 2026 using a Linux variant designed to encrypt ESXi virtual machine environments. The group deployed the ransomware, which uses ChaCha20 encryption and RSA-4096 key wrapping, by manually copying it to victim systems hosted on Cloudflare R2. Aurora operators also used a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for VMware ESXi hosts and vCenter servers by checking ports 443 and 902 and fingerprinting TLS certificates.

Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators abused Cursor Agent, which runs Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation across ten target organizations. The AI agent was tasked with standard hacking activities including installing VPN clients, scanning networks with Nmap, enumerating domain privileges, and attempting NTLM relay attacks. Researchers also identified a second Aurora cluster attributed with medium confidence that used different techniques, affecting eight victim organizations across six countries, and exfiltrated data to self-hosted S3 storage.
